main_text.p: X. Esaiæ autem 48. 11. locus sic habet, Propter me, propter me faciam, ne prophanetur nomen meum, & gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Loquitur de liberatione è carnali & spirituali Babylone. Vel igitur significat, se id facturum propter se duntaxat, non autem propter populi sui, (cuius incredulitatem & cordis duritiem eo loco exaggerat) aut alterius alicuius, iustitiam vel merita; Hanc enim gloriam ad se unum pertinere, ac sibi soli reservari oportere, ut sit simul, & is qui servat, & is propter quem servat: quæ gloria ad Christum maximè proprie pertinet. Vel, si id non significat, dicant nobis, quæso, Adversarij, quæ sit Dei sententia eo loco. Quamcunque enim aliam excogitaverint, ea, nisi vehementer fallor, aut non congruet cum verbis Dei, aut pugnabit cum illis tribus Socini responsionibus, quas jam refutavimus.

XI. Cæterum cum Deus testatur, se gloriam suam alteri non daturum, nemo est, opinor, qui non intellegat gloriam ficam[?] tum in laude, honore, cultu, adoratione, Deo debitis, tum in virtutibus gloriosissimis, ob quas cultus eiusmodi Deo debetur. Quod observo, ne quis nobis objiciat quosdam Scripturæ locos, in quibus Deus dicitur credentibus in Christum gloriam suam daturus, hoc est, salutem seu vitam æternam, quæ gloria Dei vocatur, quoniam, & præstantissima est, & Deus est illius autor, & dator.

page.notes: The upper left has a grey smudge or stain over part of paragraphs X and XI; the reading is still clear. Doubtful: "ficam[?]" in XI, which may be "sicut", "ficta" or another word; the scan is faint there. The roman numeral in the running head and in the title is read as printed, with a small mark over the X in XXVII. The ornamental rule between XI and the title block is not text and is not transcribed. The woodcut initial O is joined to OMNIA as the first word. Hyphen "ha-" at the page foot is printed, and the catchword is "habebis". Page is otherwise clean; the "Digitized by Google" watermark at the bottom right is omitted.
